why: SHADCN SWITCH'S EXACT SHAPE, and the residual an adversarial verifier left on this class's own fixed row. Tailwind v4 spells the focused switch `focus-visible:border-ring`, so examples/shadcn/contracts/switch.contract.json carries states['focus-visible'].border-{side}-color = {imported.shared.color-a1a1a1} over a resting 1px border. core/emit-figma-script.ts's applyTokens answers 'is there a border width?' from the map it was HANDED, and for a state preview that map is the DELTA — so the four opaque sides were refused with a sentence false on both counts, 'per-side border COLOURS disagree (or no border width is carried)': the sides agree, and the width is carried one plane down. The second half is the stroke write itself, gated on `spec.stroke === undefined` — an intra-call precedence rule (one Figma strokes paint; the border beats a drawn outline) that, unqualified, makes EVERY state border-colour override a silent no-op over an already-styled spec.
expectWhere: anatomy.root.states.focus-visible.border-top-color (the width stays on the resting plane, which is what a cascade is)

canvas.note: the State=Focus Visible preview must carry the REPAINTED stroke (#a1a1a1), not the resting #d4d4d8 the base cell draws. A receipt naming the channel over the WRONG value is not a wall, so this case declares mustMatch as well as mustDraw.
